# H.264 field/PAFF/MBAFF feasibility: the published reverse-engineering record

**AI disclosure:** The original research and prose were generated by Claude Code at
andreifilip123's request for [#43](https://github.com/iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video/issues/43).
Maintainer AI review corrected the evidence classification and conclusions. HerrStolzier
independently identified the geometry counterexample; original contributor commits remain.

- **Kind/date:** source-evidence reconciliation, 2026-09-17; no hardware work.
- **Decision:** keep the current kernel rejection. Firmware capability remains unresolved;
  the original reverse engineer reports a hardware limitation without a linked measurement.
- **Feeds:** [#14](https://github.com/iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video/issues/14) and
  [issue-10's design](issue-10-h264-field-mbaff.md). This answers its published-vocabulary
  search E1; it does not validate E2/E3 or promise recovery of 49 failing vectors.

## 1. Claim and history

At pinned `eiln/avd` revision `e8dfcb70dcef9fbf6cc4f11443647d9d49c3d270`, Eileen Yoon's
[README](https://github.com/eiln/avd/blob/e8dfcb70dcef9fbf6cc4f11443647d9d49c3d270/README.md#L58-L60)
places MBAFF/PAFF and top/bottom field coding under **“Unsupported by hardware.”**
This is a stronger reported claim than the kernel driver's lack of implementation.

Two README-only changes document the progression:

| Public commit | Date | Observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [a5061d1c24610ad956594cf293b29c339ab4bbc0](https://github.com/eiln/avd/commit/a5061d1c24610ad956594cf293b29c339ab4bbc0) | 2023-12-04 | Top/bottom fields listed as unverified in macOS; MBAFF/PAFF appears in a separate negative list |
| [191dcf6e75a633f363bf62d64f7c71fb1a7b908f](https://github.com/eiln/avd/commit/191dcf6e75a633f363bf62d64f7c71fb1a7b908f) | 2023-12-16 | Both become “Unsupported by hardware” |

Neither commit's message or diff links a trace, specific test sample, firmware error or
capability register. The commits establish when the public wording changed, not how the
author reached the conclusion. Private or other published evidence may exist.

The contributor searched the public issue tracker; maintainer rechecked the titles and
bodies of [issues #1](https://github.com/eiln/avd/issues/1),
[#2](https://github.com/eiln/avd/issues/2) and [#3](https://github.com/eiln/avd/issues/3)
on **2026-09-17**. These were the entries returned by the all-state GitHub issues endpoint.
No field/MBAFF hardware-capability measurement was identified in those titles/bodies.
This is a dated, limited search, not a claim about all public evidence. Issue contents are
mutable and are not pinned by a source-tree revision. Issue #3 concerns multi-reference
corruption; occurrences of field-order syntax there do not establish interlaced support.

## 2. What the reference model actually rejects

The same author's [reference-list model](https://github.com/eiln/avd/blob/e8dfcb70dcef9fbf6cc4f11443647d9d49c3d270/avid/h264/rlm.py#L197-L200)
raises `NotImplementedError` when `sl.field_pic_flag` is set, with a message attributing the
limit to hardware. This proves that this model rejects field pictures and repeats the
author's hardware claim. It is neither independent corroboration nor a silicon experiment.
MBAFF frame pictures with `field_pic_flag=0` do not trigger that guard; this guard alone
cannot classify them.

**Geometry correction:** the original PR incorrectly treated the `decoder.py` geometry
assertions as an interlace rejection. Its [pixel-height calculation](https://github.com/eiln/avd/blob/e8dfcb70dcef9fbf6cc4f11443647d9d49c3d270/avid/h264/decoder.py#L66-L70)
and [macroblock-height calculation](https://github.com/eiln/avd/blob/e8dfcb70dcef9fbf6cc4f11443647d9d49c3d270/avid/h264/decoder.py#L112-L115)
both contain `(2 - frame_mbs_only_flag)`. For the synthetic uncropped SPS
`frame_mbs_only_flag=0`, `pic_width_in_mbs_minus1=44`,
`pic_height_in_map_units_minus1=14`, the dimensions are 720×480 and 45×30 macroblocks;
both assertions pass. HerrStolzier supplied this counterexample, which the author and
maintainer re-derived. The assertions are not an unconditional rejection of interlace-capable
SPSs. This arithmetic check is not evidence that fields decode correctly.

## 3. Published kernel vocabulary

Kernel pin: `AsahiLinux/linux@94fb23346d522edf53722357c426a3e58030beea`.
The [SPS validator](https://github.com/AsahiLinux/linux/blob/94fb23346d522edf53722357c426a3e58030beea/drivers/media/platform/apple/avd/avd-h264.c#L572-L585)
rejects a cleared `V4L2_H264_SPS_FLAG_FRAME_MBS_ONLY` with `-EINVAL`. Its
“no interlaced support” comment establishes current driver behavior. No separately measured
hardware-capability evidence is cited there. The driver credits the original RE lineage;
independence of this conclusion is unestablished.

Two different definitions must be distinguished:

- [Reference-list opcode](https://github.com/AsahiLinux/linux/blob/94fb23346d522edf53722357c426a3e58030beea/drivers/media/platform/apple/avd/avd-inst.h#L103-L107):
  `AVD_OP_REF` carries `AVD_OP_REF_DBP_IDX`, `AVD_OP_REF_LOOP_IDX` and
  `AVD_OP_REF_LIST_IDX` (the source spells it `DBP`).
- [Reference-table header](https://github.com/AsahiLinux/linux/blob/94fb23346d522edf53722357c426a3e58030beea/drivers/media/platform/apple/avd/avd-inst.h#L149-L152):
  `AVD_REF_NUM`, `AVD_REF_FLAG_CONST`, `AVD_REF_FLAG_LONG` and `AVD_REF_DELTA_POC`.
  These are not the fields of the reference-list opcode.

No identified parity/pairing encoding was found in these published definitions. That is a
bounded source observation, not an exhaustive description of firmware commands or proof
that no such encoding exists. The kernel macro `FIELD_PREP` itself refers to bitfields,
not video field pictures. See [issue-10's source map](issue-10-h264-field-mbaff.md#9-evidence-appendix)
for the earlier multi-layer analysis; this PR does not revalidate all those layers.

| Claim | Classification and exact evidence | Missing fact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original RE author reports hardware does not support MBAFF/PAFF or field coding | Attributed report: [pinned README](https://github.com/eiln/avd/blob/e8dfcb70dcef9fbf6cc4f11443647d9d49c3d270/README.md#L58-L60), [wording-change commit](https://github.com/eiln/avd/commit/191dcf6e75a633f363bf62d64f7c71fb1a7b908f) | Linked measurement and its hardware/firmware identity |
| The author's model rejects field pictures | Source-observed: [RLM guard](https://github.com/eiln/avd/blob/e8dfcb70dcef9fbf6cc4f11443647d9d49c3d270/avid/h264/rlm.py#L197-L200) | Does not test silicon or establish rejection of MBAFF-only frame pictures |
| Current AVD driver rejects interlace-capable SPSs | Source-observed: [validator](https://github.com/AsahiLinux/linux/blob/94fb23346d522edf53722357c426a3e58030beea/drivers/media/platform/apple/avd/avd-h264.c#L572-L585) | Whether a correct alternative command/reference contract is possible |
| No identified parity/pairing encoding in the inspected command definitions | Bounded source observation: [list opcode](https://github.com/AsahiLinux/linux/blob/94fb23346d522edf53722357c426a3e58030beea/drivers/media/platform/apple/avd/avd-inst.h#L103-L107), [table header](https://github.com/AsahiLinux/linux/blob/94fb23346d522edf53722357c426a3e58030beea/drivers/media/platform/apple/avd/avd-inst.h#L149-L152) | Unmapped firmware vocabulary, if any |
| Firmware/silicon field capability is established either way | **Unresolved** from these sources | Attributable hardware-success evidence or a validated capability/command contract; failure of an incomplete driver is insufficient |

## 5. Decision and next bounded step

Keep #14 blocked. Issue-10's “missing validated encoding, not proof of firmware incapability”
classification remains appropriate. Cite the original author's explicit hardware-limit report
alongside it. Do not assign a probability of hardware impossibility from this record.

Before implementing field decoding, obtain a validated parity/pairing/reference contract or
prepare a separately reviewed experiment with one falsifiable hypothesis. A properly
attributed macOS **hardware** success result or trace (distinguishing software fallback),
with SoC, firmware, stream syntax and exact output, could discriminate capability. That route
is not excluded merely because this source search found no such evidence.

The old E2/E3 suggestions are research prompts requiring a complete test and safety design;
relaxing the SPS rejection alone cannot establish a valid command contract. A failed decode
through an incomplete experimental driver cannot prove silicon incapability. A source-only
stop pending better evidence is acceptable and is the decision here. No upstream contact,
module change or hardware experiment is requested or performed by this PR.

## 6. Validation and acceptance

Verified the two full README-history commits, pinned RLM guard, distinct kernel reference
families, validator and synthetic geometry counterexample. Documentation links and required
companion Bash/rebuild baseline checked during integration; no new runtime test is needed
for this prose-only change. Original research ran on macOS; maintainer source review ran
on Linux. No firmware capture, decode, kernel build, module load or installation.

#43's four criteria are met as source research: the reported claim is reconciled (sections
1–3), immutable evidence and missing facts are tabulated (4), no device/tool is required,
and the bounded stop/next evidence gate is explicit (5). #14, support tables and the failing
49-vector set remain unchanged. Completion of #43 does not make #14 claimable.
